title: Cash refunds at the register always fail (regression from round 1)
description: Round 1 replaced the old change check with `const cash = sum of CASH tenders; ... if (totals.change > cash) throw new UserError("Only cash gives change...")`. On a refund (total < 0), every tender has to be negative, so `cash` is negative whenever any cash is paid out, while `totals.change` is always 0 for refunds. `0 > negative` is true, so any refund that includes a cash tender is rejected. The client never checks this: it enables "Complete refund" as soon as paid === total. Paying a customer back in cash from the drawer, the usual way returns are settled at a fabric or notions counter, cannot be done. The only workaround is recording the refund as Card, Check or Other, which puts the wrong figures in the register-sales report's "Taken in" by-method totals and the cash-drawer count. Before 8b3e5f2 the check was `totals.change > 0 && !tenders.some(CASH)`, which never fired on a refund.
failure_scenario: Owner or staff turns on Return mode, scans QA-SPOOL-1 ($4.99 + 6.35% tax = $5.31 refund), clicks Cash (tender -531), then clicks Complete refund. The toast reads "Only cash gives change. Take the exact amount on the card or check." and nothing is saved. The same refund recorded as Card goes through.
suggested_fix: Apply the check only to sales: `if (totals.total >= 0 && totals.change > cash) throw ...` (or compare against `Math.max(0, cash)`). Add an e2e test or a register-math unit test covering a cash refund, a card refund and a mixed exchange.
evidence:
UI reproduction (Playwright, own throwaway shop, script ui-refund.cjs):
  total shown: $5.31
  Complete refund enabled: true
  toast: Only cash gives change. Take the exact amount on the card or check.
Server action replay (t2.mjs, completeSale id 40f3cfdb8afc...):
  owner cash refund {"error":"Only cash gives change. Take the exact amount on the card or check."}
  owner card refund {"saleId":"cmuinde370040ah7dp0stth87","number":1002,"changeCents":0}
Code: register.ts:220 `const cash = tenders.filter((t) => t.method === "CASH").reduce(...)`, then :222 `if (totals.change > cash) throw ...`. There is no e2e or unit test for returns or refunds (grep for "refund"/"Return mode" in tests/ finds nothing).
verifier_notes:
confirmed: The description of the code is accurate. saleTotals() (register-math.ts:33) returns change = 0 whenever total < 0. For a refund, line 219 forces every tender to be <= 0, so `cash` (line 220) is negative as soon as one CASH tender exists. Line 222 `if (totals.change > cash)` then reads 0 > -531 and throws. A refund paid only by card, check or other has cash = 0 and passes. Round 1 (8b3e5f2) caused this: its diff replaced `totals.change > 0 && !tenders.some(CASH)` with this line. The client (register.tsx:499) enables "Complete refund" once paid === total and never runs this check. So every refund or net-negative exchange paid back in cash fails with a misleading "Only cash gives change" toast. The only workaround is to record the refund as another method, which puts wrong figures in the by-method totals and the drawer count. No test covers returns or refunds. I rate it high because a routine POS flow is broken outright and the only workaround records the wrong tender.
confirmed: The code does what the reviewer says. In saleTotals (src/lib/register-math.ts:33), `change` is `total >= 0 ? max(0, paid - total) : 0`, so it is always 0 on a refund. completeSale (src/actions/register.ts:219) first requires every tender on a refund to be negative, so `cash` (line 220) is negative whenever a cash tender is present. The unconditional check `if (totals.change > cash)` at line 222 then evaluates `0 > negative`, which is true, and it throws. The same happens for a mixed card+cash refund. For sales (total >= 0), line 221 already guarantees paid - total <= cash with cash >= 0, so line 222 can never fire on a sale. The line only does harm, and only on refunds. It came in with 8b3e5f2: the diff replaced `totals.change > 0 && !tenders.some(CASH)`, which could not fire on a refund, with the unguarded comparison. 9ba25a4 did not change it. The client (register.tsx:111-115, 499) turns cash into a negative tender and enables Complete refund as soon as paid === total, so nothing stops the user before the server rejects it. The only way through is recording the refund as Card, Check or Other, which puts wrong by-method totals in the drawer and sales reports. No test in tests/ or scripts/ mentions a refund or Return mode. Severity: the cash-refund path of the register is completely blocked, and the workaround misstates money by tender method. That is a core register flow broken plus wrong money figures, so high. It is a correctness regression, not a security hole.
also_reported_as: code: src/actions/register.ts:222 Every cash refund at the register is rejected with "Only cash gives change" (regression from round 1)

title: The tech-role price lock at the register can be bypassed with a 100% line or whole-sale discount; unpriced items sell at $0
description:
Round 1 added 'Only an owner or admin can change the price' for TECH users. The server checks unit price only. The UI disables the Price field but leaves 'Disc %' and 'Discount on the whole sale' enabled, and the server accepts any discount (line 179: `disc = Math.max(0, Math.round(Number(l.discountCents ?? 0)))`) and any order discount (line 216) from a TECH. A tech can therefore sell anything for $0, consigned stock included, which also reports a $0 price to the consigning partner.

For an item with no price, the server lets a TECH set one (`part.priceCents != null && ...`), but the client disables the Price field for TECH. The item goes on the sale at $0 while the toast tells the clerk to 'Type the price on the line'.

The same gap exists for repair tickets: removePayment was made admin-only 'like voiding a register sale' (tickets.ts:370), but a TECH can add a negative payment of the same amount through addPayment (tickets.ts:353-357), with the same effect.
failure_scenario: Sign in as TECH, scan QALAST ($25.00) and set Disc % to 100, then scan QANOPRICE (no price). Total is $0.00, Complete sale is enabled, and sale #1002 is saved. On the ticket page, the TECH enters -25 as the amount, clicks Record payment, and gets 'Payment recorded'.
suggested_fix: In completeSale, when user.role === 'TECH', reject non-zero discountCents and orderDiscountCents, or cap them at a shop-configured maximum. Allow a TECH to set a price only when part.priceCents == null, and enable the client Price field for that case, e.g. `disabled={(!canSell && l.priceWasSet) || ...}`. In addPayment, require an admin for amounts < 0.
evidence: Playwright t2.js as qa-reg-tech: `price disabled? true`, `disc disabled? false`, `TOASTS [ 'QANOPRICE has no price. Type the price on the line.' ]`, `noprice price disabled? true`, `Total | $0.00`, `DONE Sale #1002 done.` Export row: `1002,...,QALAST,Last one scissors,1,25.00,25.00,0.00`. t13.js: a Payment row `CARD | -2500 | tech refund` was created by the TECH user.
verifier_notes: confirmed: register.ts:191 checks only unitPriceCents for TECH. Line discounts (line 179, capped only at the line amount) and the order discount (line 216) are unrestricted, and the client leaves Disc % and 'Discount on the whole sale' enabled for TECH, so a 100% discount gets around the round-1 price lock. The unpriced-item bug is a concrete functional defect: the server would accept a TECH-set price when part.priceCents == null, but register.tsx:353 disables the Price field whenever !canSell. The toast tells the TECH to type the price, yet the item can only go through at $0. The negative ticket payment is also real (addPayment, tickets.ts:353-357, has no sign check for TECH). It is weaker than claimed, though: unlike removePayment it leaves a visible row. Context that limits severity: TECH is a same-shop employee, and ticket DISCOUNT lines and misc-item returns are also open to TECH, so the register price lock is more a guard than a hard boundary. This is not cross-shop escalation, so medium, not high.
also_reported_as: security: src/actions/register.ts:191 A tech (lowest role) can get around the owner/admin-only money controls: any-amount refunds, 100% discounts, reversing payments
security: src/actions/register.ts:191 Register 'only owner/admin can change the price' control is ineffective: a TECH can sell at any price via discounts, and can edit part prices directly
code: src/actions/register.ts:191 Tech-role price lock is bypassable: techs can give 100% discounts and pay out arbitrary misc/return refunds

title: Scanning an exact part number rings up a different cross-referenced item when the exact one shows 0 on hand (round-1 regression)
description: Round 1 replaced 'exact partNumber first, then numberKeys' with a single ranking: `(p.qtyOnHand > 0 ? 0 : 4) + (p.consignLinkId ? 2 : 0) + (exact(p) ? 0 : 1)`. It was meant for an own item versus a consigned twin, but it applies to every numberKeys match. Being in stock (weight 4) outweighs being the exact number (weight 1), so any other part that lists the scanned number as an alt number wins whenever the exact item's count is 0 or negative. The register then silently charges the other item's price and decrements the wrong item's stock. The register never blocks overselling, so counts at or below 0 are common.
failure_scenario: QALAST ($25.00 scissors, qtyOnHand 0) and QAGENERIC ($9.99, qtyOnHand 5, altNumbers ['QALAST']). Scanning the barcode QALAST puts 'QAGENERIC Generic scissors $9.99' on the sale. The customer is undercharged $15.01, QAGENERIC's stock drops, and QALAST's does not.
suggested_fix: Rank an exact partNumber match first. Apply the stock/consigned preference only among candidates that are the same item (the own/consigned twins created by import, e.g. same consignItemKey or partNumber vs 'partNumber (own)'). For example: `rank = (exact?0:8) + (qty>0?0:4) + (consigned?2:0)`, special-casing the twin pair.
evidence: Playwright t16.js: `rows: ... QAGENERICGeneric scissors (fits same) $9.99` after scanning 'QALAST'. The pre-round-1 code (git show 8b3e5f2) looked up `partNumber equals c` first.
verifier_notes: confirmed: itemByCode's rank at register.ts:60 weights stock (4) above an exact partNumber match (1). Any part that lists the scanned number in its numberKeys (cross-reference alt numbers) and has stock beats the exact part when the exact part's count is 0 or less. The doc comment states the intent as own stock versus a partner's consigned twin, but the ranking applies to all cross-references. Before round 1 (git show 8b3e5f2) the exact partNumber was looked up first, so this is a regression. The register silently substitutes a different item, with a different price and stock. It needs a cross-reference plus a count at or below 0; the register never blocks overselling, so zero counts are common. A less common flow, hence medium.

title: A whole-sale discount is not passed on to consigned items: the consigning partner is credited the undiscounted price
description: Consigned lines count toward the whole-sale discount base (discountable is true and lineNet > 0), so the customer pays less for them. The consign.sale message and the ConsignSale row, however, use `Math.round(lineNet(l) / l.qty)`, which applies the line discount but not the whole-sale discount. The register sales report's 'Consigned stock sold' uses the same pre-discount amount. The partner terms describe the shop's share as a share of 'what consigned stock sells for', and a line discount is passed through, so the two discount kinds are treated inconsistently.
failure_scenario: A consigned $24.00 cutter is sold with 50% off the whole sale, so the customer pays $12.00 plus tax. The repair shop is credited 1 x $24.00, and at the 30% share the sewing shop owes $16.80, more than it took in for the item.
suggested_fix: Allocate the whole-sale discount to each eligible line in proportion, as the tax reduction already does, and use the allocated net for consigned lines. Alternatively, state in the terms and UI that whole-sale discounts come out of the shop's own share.
evidence: Static reading. saleTotals applies orderDiscount across `eligible` lines, which include consigned lines. The consignSale create (lines 264-277) and the sendToPartner payload (line 285) use `lineNet(l) / l.qty` only. Not run end to end: it needs a hub partnership.
verifier_notes: confirmed: Consigned lines are in the whole-sale discount base: saleTotals uses `eligible` with discountable !== false, and consigned parts are discountable. ConsignSale.priceCents, shopKeepsCents and the consign.sale payload, however, use lineNet/qty, which drops the whole-sale discount (register.ts:264-285). The partner statement (partners.ts:1209-1211) then owes the owner gross - keeps based on the undiscounted price. The terms say the shop keeps a share of 'what consigned stock sells for', and a line discount is passed through, so the two discount kinds disagree. The result is wrong partner-settlement money every time a whole-sale discount covers consigned items (a less common but ordinary flow, e.g. guild or coupon discounts). No docs describe it as intended.

title: completeSale stores an unlimited number of tenders per sale
description: Sale lines are capped at 300, but input.tenders is not capped. Each tender (with up to 100 characters of note) goes into the sale's JSON column and is later parsed and joined on every render of /register/sales and the receipt. The server-action body limit is 16 MB, so any signed-in user of a shop can store hundreds of thousands of tenders on one sale and slow down that shop's sales pages and exports.
failure_scenario: A signed-in user replays completeSale with 5,000 one-cent CASH tenders for a $50 sale. It is accepted and stored, and the register-sales list and receipt render all 5,000 entries.
suggested_fix: Reject more than about 10 tenders (throw new UserError("Too many payments on one sale.")), and make sure note is a string before slicing (typeof t.note === "string").
evidence: t10.mjs -> {"saleId":"cmuinjq7m00lcah7dhblznpgu","number":1007,...}; psql: jsonb_array_length(tenders)=5000, pg_column_size=16420 (sale 1007, own shop).
verifier_notes: plausible: Accurate. input.tenders is not capped (register.ts:213-215), unlike lines (max 300), and serverActions.bodySizeLimit is 16mb (next.config.ts), which allows about 470k tenders per sale. The reviewer's 5000-tender sale is stored. The impact can reach past the reviewer's own-shop slowdown. The register-sales export (export/[what]/route.ts:51-56) builds one `paid` string from every tender and repeats it on each of the sale's lines, so output grows with lines x tenders. In my mirror of that code, a 1 MB request (30k tenders, 300 lines) gives a 108 MB CSV and about 222 MB of heap in one request. At the 16 MB limit this would pass V8's maximum string length and very likely exhaust memory in the shared Node process. On a hosted multi-shop install any shop owner could then take the app down for every shop (railway.json restarts only 5 times). I did not trigger this against a live server: it would load the shared machine. I rate it medium as a DoS that needs a login. A non-string note makes `t.note?.slice` throw, which only produces a 500.

title: A partner repair paid at the sewing shop's counter locks in the sewing shop's cached bill: a later or unsynced change to the repair shop's bill can't be collected or refunded
description: The register charges repairDue(job) from the sewing shop's local copy of the job (totalCents from the last job.update it received), then sets job.paidAt and sends job.paid. From then on everything treats the job as settled. pickupJobs() filters `paidAt: null`. completeSale refuses 'Repair tag X is already paid.' (register.ts:170). The sewing-shop job.update handler keeps the existing paidAt (partners.ts:786). The repair-side job.paid handler accepts only the first payment (partners.ts:821). The repair shop's jobSnapshot keeps job.paidAt (partners.ts:363). The repairs page shows 'Paid <date>'. If the repair shop's bill changed after the sewing shop's last sync, the difference stays on the repair shop's ticket as an unpaid (or overpaid) balance. That happens with a part added after 'ready', or during the offline mode added in round 2, or in the one-minute sync gap. Neither shop's register can collect or refund it, and the customer has already left with the machine.
failure_scenario: The repair shop marks tag 1042 Ready ($120), which reaches the sewing shop. The tech then adds a $35 part to the ticket, while the sewing shop is offline or the next partner sync hasn't run. The customer pays $120 at the sewing shop's register and takes the machine. The sewing shop sees 'Paid'. The repair shop's ticket shows $35 + tax still owed, which no register flow can collect, and the commission was fixed at the $120 bill.
suggested_fix: When a job.update arrives for a paid job whose totalCents - repairPaidCents - paidCents != 0, surface the difference: keep a 'balance after payment' field, list such jobs in Repair pickup (or a to-do) with the extra due or refund, and allow a second job.paid for the difference instead of ignoring it. Alternatively have the sewing shop confirm the current bill with the hub before charging when it's online.
evidence: register.ts:97 pickupJobs `paidAt: null`; :170 `if (j.paidAt) throw ... already paid`; :186 `unit = repairDue(job)` from the local row; register.ts:291-303 sets paidAt and sends job.paid once; partners.ts:786 `...(paidAt && !job.paidAt ? ...)` never clears paidAt; partners.ts:821 `if (job.paidWhere === "shop" || job.paidWhere === "split") return;`; repairs/[id]/page.tsx:103 shows 'Paid' with no remaining amount.

title: Complete sale fails silently on any server error, and nothing stops a duplicate sale when the cashier retries
description: finish() uses try/finally with no catch. completeSale returns { error } only for UserError; everything else rejects the promise, and the button just switches back to "Complete sale" with no toast. Examples: a Prisma error such as an Int overflow or P2025 when a part is deleted mid-sale, a transaction timeout, the hosted server being unreachable, or a lost response. The cart is still there, so the cashier clicks again. completeSale has no idempotency key, so if the first call committed and only the response was lost, the retry creates a second sale, decrements stock twice and queues a second consign.sale to the partner under new line ids. The unit price also has no upper bound, so a typo such as 30000000 overflows the Int columns and hits this silent path.
failure_scenario: Owner adds a misc item priced 30000000 with a Card tender and clicks Complete sale. The server logs 'Value out of range ... "3000000000" is out of range for type integer'. The UI shows no toast and no status; the button is back to 'Complete sale' with the cart unchanged. The same silent result occurs when the network drops during a sale.
suggested_fix: Add `catch { toast.error("The sale wasn't saved (no connection or a server problem). Check Register sales before ringing it again.") }` in finish(), and similar handling in lookup and pickupJobs. Generate a client key (crypto.randomUUID()) per cart, send it with completeSale, store it on Sale with @@unique([shopId, clientKey]), and on a unique conflict return the existing sale. Bound unitPriceCents and qty*unit to a sane maximum (e.g. MAX_MONEY) with a UserError.
evidence: register.tsx:119-153: `async function finish() { setBusy(true); try { const r = await completeSale({...}); if ("error" in r) {...} ... } finally { setBusy(false); } }` (no catch). register.ts:313-316 rethrows non-UserErrors. Playwright: 'CONSOLE: Failed to load resource: ... 500', 'PAGEERROR: An error occurred in the Server Components render...', 'toasts: []', 'status: []', 'button: Complete sale'. bench-server.log:545 'Value out of range for the type: value "3000000000" is out of range for type integer'.
verifier_notes: confirmed: finish() in register.tsx has try/finally and no catch. completeSale returns {error} only for UserErrors and rethrows everything else (register.ts:313-316). Any server error, a failed fetch or a lost response therefore becomes an unhandled rejection: no toast, the button resets and the cart is kept. Worse, the stale 'Sale #N done' status from the previous sale stays on screen, because adding a misc item doesn't clear `done`, so the failed attempt can look like a success. There is no upper bound on unitPriceCents (toCents is unbounded), so a typo overflows the Int columns and lands on this silent path. completeSale also has no idempotency key, so retrying after a committed-but-lost response would create a second sale and decrement stock twice. That part follows from the code but was not reproduced.
also_reported_as: qa: src/components/register.tsx:121 Unexpected server errors leave the clerk with no message: a mistyped tender causes an Int overflow 500, and completeSale has no input bounds

title: A handheld scanner types into whatever field has focus, so scanned items are silently lost or change another line's discount or yardage
description: The scan box only gets focus when the page loads, after a search result or misc item is added, and after a sale. After the clerk edits a line's Qty, Price or Disc % field, or clicks a tender button, focus stays there. A keyboard-wedge scanner types its code and presses Enter into the focused element. In the Qty field (type=number) the digits are appended to the yardage. In Disc % they are clamped to 100, so the line becomes free. On a focused tender button, Enter clicks it again and adds a tender for the balance. In every case the scanned item is never added. README/INSTALL promise that any scanner that 'types the code and presses Enter works in the register's scan box', and 'scan the bolt, type the yardage, scan the next item' is the core fabric flow. The server does not catch any of this: it accepts any fractional yardage (only non-yd items must be whole numbers) and any discount.
failure_scenario: (1) Scan QAFAB, type 2.375 in its Qty field, then scan the next item (UPC 012345678905). The qty becomes 2.375012345678905 (still shown as '2 3/8 yd') and the second item is never rung up. (2) Type 10 in a line's Disc % field, then scan. The field becomes 100 and the line shows $0.00. Complete sale is enabled for a $0.00 total. (3) Type 3, click Card, then scan. No item is added and a second Card tender of $2.32 is recorded even though the card was never run.
suggested_fix: Route scanner bursts to the scan box: add a window keydown listener that treats fast keystrokes ending in Enter as a scan (by inter-key timing) and calls lookup(), wherever focus is. Also return focus to #register-code after addTender and after a qty/price/discount edit is committed (on Enter or blur). On both client and server, round yard quantities to the eighth and reject anything else: `Math.abs(qty*8 - Math.round(qty*8)) > 1e-9`.
evidence:
Reproduced with Playwright on :3100 (scratchpad scripts t19.js, t20.js, t11.js).
- t20: `qty value: 2.375012345678905` / rows show only `Kona cotton white 2 3/8 yd $30.85`.
- t19: `disc value: 100` / `Kona cotton white 1 yd $0.00` / `Total $0.00`.
- t11: `focused: <button ...>Card</button>`, then after typing QAFAB+Enter the tenders read `Card $3.00 | Card $2.32` and no fabric line.

Code: `onChange={(e) => setLine(l.key, { qty: Number(e.target.value) })}` (line 344); `discountPct: Math.min(100, Math.max(0, Number(e.target.value) || 0))` (line 367); addTender (lines 111-117) leaves focus on the button. The only refocus calls are at lines 55, 149, 215 and 245.
verifier_notes:
confirmed: The code does what the report says. The only calls that refocus #register-code are at register.tsx:55, 149, 215 and 245. None follows a Qty/Price/Disc % edit or addTender. The sale table and the tender buttons are not inside a form, so a scanner's burst plus Enter goes into whatever field has focus: digits are appended to a number input, and Enter re-clicks a focused button. The server accepts any fractional yd qty (register.ts:190 checks whole numbers only for non-yd items) and any discount. I reproduced all three cases independently. I rate it medium, not high: every effect shows on screen before Complete sale (no line added, a $0.00 line, an extra tender row), and the app's own beep does not fire. Also, INSTALL.md literally promises the scanner works 'in the register's scan box', which is true when that box has focus. It is still a real bug in the common fabric flow (type the yardage, then scan the next bolt), and a missed item is an undercharge.
confirmed: The description of the code is accurate. The scan box #register-code is only refocused at register.tsx:55 (mount), :149 (after a sale), :215 (after picking a search result) and :245 (after adding a misc item). There is no window keydown or scanner-burst handler anywhere in src (grep for keydown/onKeyDown finds nothing). After a Qty, Disc % or Price edit, or a click on a tender button, a keyboard-wedge scan goes into that element.

On the server, completeSale (src/actions/register.ts:175-190) only requires a finite qty with 0 < |qty| <= 10000 and whole numbers for non-yd items, so any fractional yardage is stored. qtyText/yards() rounds to eighths for display, which hides the stray digits on the line and the receipt. Neither prior round (8b3e5f2 or 9ba25a4) touched focus handling. No spec exercises the register scan flow.

I reproduced every scenario independently on :3100 with my own shop:
- Qty: after typing yardage, a scanned UPC is appended to the Qty field, the second item is never rung up, and the fractional qty is saved to the sale and to inventory.
- Disc %: after typing 10, a scan clamps the field to 100, the line becomes $0.00, and Complete sale is enabled.
- Tender: after clicking Card, a scan's Enter records a second Card tender for the balance.
- Tab away first: focus lands in the Price field and the item is still lost.

I rate it medium, not high:
- Every outcome is visible before Complete sale: the item is missing from the cart, there is no success beep, the line shows $0.00, and a second tender row appears.
- The scanner still works once the clerk clicks the scan box. INSTALL.md:213 promises it 'works in the register's scan box', which is literally true.
- The stray yardage digits change the money by less than a cent.

Still, fabric-by-the-yard sales hit this constantly: every cut needs a Qty edit, and the natural next step is to scan the next item. That can lose revenue (items not charged, lines made free), cause inventory drift and record wrong tenders. The server also stores yardage that isn't in eighths, which is missing validation that saves bad data. That is more than a minor edge case.

title: Sales log totals leave out closed tickets returned unrepaired, so their taxable diagnosis fees and tax are missing
description: Service, Labor, Parts, 'Sales tax' and commission on /sales come only from tickets with status COLLECTED closed in the range. setStatus also closes RETURNED_UNREPAIRED (and ABANDONED) tickets. The default service menu has 'Diagnosis & estimate' at $49, and SERVICE lines are taxable by default (TicketLine.taxable @default(true); addLine SERVICE doesn't override it). So a declined estimate billed and paid on a returned-unrepaired machine shows up in 'Money taken' but not in 'Sales tax' or 'Service'. The tax figure the owner files from is understated.
failure_scenario: Customer declines the estimate. The ticket bills 'Diagnosis & estimate' $49 + 6% tax = $51.94 and is paid, then marked RETURNED_UNREPAIRED. On /sales, 'Money taken' includes $51.94, but 'Sales tax' omits the $2.94 and 'Service (collected)' omits the $49.
suggested_fix: Select tickets by `closedAt` in range with `status: { in: ["COLLECTED", "RETURNED_UNREPAIRED", "ABANDONED"] }` (or any status whose ticket has lines), and rename the tiles from '(collected)' to '(closed)'. Note separately: reopened tickets keep their old closedAt (DB shows ON_BENCH tickets with closedAt set), so their work is dated to the first close.
evidence: sales/page.tsx:17-20 `db.ticket.findMany({ where: { shopId: user.shopId, status: "COLLECTED", closedAt: { gte: start, lt: end } }, ...` ; tickets.ts:147-148 closes COLLECTED, RETURNED_UNREPAIRED and ABANDONED; service-menu.ts:17 'Diagnosis & estimate ... 4900'; schema.prisma:343 TicketLine `taxable Boolean @default(true)`; register.ts:97 pickupJobs treats RETURNED_UNREPAIRED as billable.
verifier_notes: confirmed: setStatus (tickets.ts:147-148) sets closedAt for COLLECTED, RETURNED_UNREPAIRED and ABANDONED. The /sales page computes Service, Labor, Parts, Sales tax and commission only from tickets with status COLLECTED (sales/page.tsx:17-20), while 'Money taken' sums every payment by paidAt. SERVICE lines are created without a taxable override, so they take the schema default taxable=true (schema.prisma TicketLine; tickets.ts only sets taxable for FEE/DISCOUNT). The default menu includes 'Diagnosis & estimate' at $4900 and a storage fee. A declined repair that bills the diagnosis fee and is marked RETURNED_UNREPAIRED therefore shows its payment in Money taken but not in the 'Sales tax' tile. That tile has no '(collected)' qualifier and is the only repair-side tax figure in the app.
